date_note: Publication day of the ITSitio article (20 November), the earliest source read; neither source gives an earlier date for the campaign.
title: Avast researchers: PDF promising GTA VI download delivers an infostealer
geo_basis: researcher HQ; neither source names a victim country
summary: Guia de TI and ITSitio, each citing Avast research, report a PDF that promises the full GTA VI game and links to a site with a download button. The button leads to a fake Google Drive-style page offering a ZIP file of over 700 MB, which the articles say carries an infostealer that takes credentials and other information stored on the device.
plain: A PDF that claims to offer the full GTA VI game leads to a fake download page. The file is said to carry malware that steals saved logins and other data.
exec: A game-lure infostealer, as reported from Avast research, targets consumers' stored credentials and other information.
action: Per Avast as reported, avoid downloads from links in PDFs, forums, social media or unknown sites, buy games only from official stores and keep security software updated.

evidence.quote: un archivo ZIP de más de 700 MB

validation.note: ITSitio (20 Nov) and Guia de TI (21 Nov) both relay the same Avast research; Avast's own post was not read, so the finding rests on one party. Place changed from Brazil (assumed from the publisher's language) to Avast as researcher: neither article names a victim country.

review.note: exec added an unsourced consequence (work devices); now restates the summary only. Title, Avast attribution, 700 MB and advice match both articles; place already fixed to Avast HQ
